newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand irritated by Malaysian newspaper cartoons.
newsitem.headline: Thailand irritated by Malaysian newspaper cartoons.

text.p: Thailand on Wednesday complained about two cartoons which appeared in Malaysian newspapers, saying the images did not create a conducive atmosphere for a meeting of ASEAN nations later this week.

A senior Foreign Ministry official said in a statement on Wednesday that Thailand and its people were "saddened and disappointed" after the cartoons were published in the New Sunday Times and its daily the New Straits Times this week.

Ministry spokesman Surapong Jayanama said the controversial cartoons were motivated by the current squabbling between Malaysia and Singapore, and accused the Malaysian press of trying to drag Thailand into the conflict.
"Despite the fact that Thailand has nothing to do with the conflict of the two countries, the Malaysian press are trying to drag it into the Malaysia-Singapore row," he said.

"This makes the Thai government and its people saddened and disappointed. Such an act has given a negative impact to the good image of the country and any friendly countries should not have done this to each other," he said.

Ties between Singapore and Malaysia took a dive earlier this year after Lee made disparaging remarks about the southern Malaysian state of Johor, saying it was "notorious for shootings, muggins and car-jacking."

One cartoon depicted a group of Singaporeans queuing at an immigration checkpoint waiting to tour Thailand and Indonesia, while a man resembling Singaporean Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew was shown distributing condoms and reminding the crowd not to forget to use them when on holiday in the two countries.
The other cartoon depicted Singaporean tourists going through an AIDS checkpoint on their return home from Thailand.
"...The Thai government and people fully regret and are disappointed that they were being drawn into the issue which affected Thailand's image, Surapong said in the statement.

"It goes against normal practices of friendly countries and especially in this case did not create a conducive atmosphere for welcoming foreign ministers from friendly countries like Thailand who is due to attend the May 31 meeting in Kuala Lumpur," Surapong said.

Foreign ministers from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations -- which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam and Thailand -- are to meet at the weekend to discuss whether or not to accept Burma, Laos and Cambodia as members.

Thailand, which has a thriving sex industry, has been praised by UNAIDS officials for its successful in campaign in boosting usage of condom to curb and preventing the further spread of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
